notes:
Passed on the fake backend with python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model and reviewed_by is null; no hardware was attached or run. The card names five entry symbols; this package implements the first confirmed one, robust_gymnasium.envs.classic_control.cartpole:CartPoleEnv (CartPole-v1), and names the other four (MountainCarEnv, Continuous_MountainCarEnv, PendulumEnv, AcrobotEnv) in facts.md without implementing them. The fake backend is the package's pure Python re-implementation of the clone's equations and the 500-step time limit; it was not compared with the upstream environment, and neither robust_gymnasium nor gymnasium was installed where the gate ran. The bridge's unlisted sim path calls gymnasium.make('CartPole-v1'), i.e. the base Gymnasium distribution rather than robust_gymnasium.make, so only the fake backend is provided and checked; the sim path was not run. The install block in driver.lock.json is the card's and was not run. Two kinds of warnings are expected of a Gymnasium family driver and remain: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only configures the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT warnings for the bridge-derived integer inputs (ticks, action.index and seed in reset and seed). There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings and no catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
